reviews.decision_reason: select_demand preserves the available corpus records selected by the threshold/fallback path; the supplied runtime preview shows selected_df and the returned DataFrame both have 8 rows, matching the 8-row input corpus and keeping explicit identifiers available for downstream processing.

normalize is the behaviorally significant fault. It hard-codes index_window = [0] and returns only head(1), collapsing the 8 selected/retained demand records to a single need. This removes supported demand records needed for downstream coverage and priority evaluation, leaving missing evidence invisible rather than preserving bounded normalized needs.

assemble_provenance deterministically ranks the normalized input it receives using demand_score descending and record_id as a tiebreaker, with missing-safe field access. Its one-row evidence_sources output follows from the faulty one-row normalized input, so the defect is upstream in normalize rather than in provenance assembly.
